name: ninja-forms
notes: DUO-3222 (version-pinned adapter compatibility contract): plugin/version_range verified live (not guessed) — ninja-forms/ninja-forms.php, re-confirmed at 3.14.11 this session (unchanged from the typed-snapshot grounding below — same version, re-verified independently). Range scoped to the CURRENT major line only (3.x, [3.0.0, 4.0.0)) — widening to cover other major versions is DUO-3224's ratification job, not invented here.

Task #75 CLOSED (was: Grind R1-A's honest-partial marker). This manifest now captures a Ninja Forms form's actual content — nf3_forms/nf3_fields/nf3_actions + their _meta twins — via the typed-snapshot grammar in agent/src/Snapshot.php. Real schema DESCRIBE'd live on NF 3.14.11 again for THIS implementation (not reused from the R1-A report's summary alone): nf3_forms has 14 columns (id, title, key, created_at, updated_at, views, subs, form_title, default_label_pos, show_title, clear_complete, hide_complete, logged_in, seq_num); nf3_fields.parent_id and nf3_actions.parent_id are PLAIN single-target integer FKs into nf3_forms.id, confirmed via SHOW CREATE TABLE to carry no real FOREIGN KEY constraint at all (ordinary WordPress-plugin practice) — so a phase-1 placeholder of 0 is always safe. nf3_forms.key was empirically NULL on the live Job Application fixture, contradicting task #75's own one-line speculation that it might serve as a natural key — mapped identity is used for all three tables. Because plugin rows cannot carry `_duo_uuid`, durability is supplied by duo_map plus the versioned, database-matched identity recovery sidecar; populated restores without it block rather than minting or rebinding identities (DUO-3209).

A genuinely important empirical finding, not assumed: nf3_form_meta/nf3_field_meta/nf3_action_meta DUPLICATE a large fraction of their owning row's real COLUMNS as mirrored meta KEYS of the same name (e.g. nf3_field_meta carries 'label'/'key'/'type'/'order'/'label_pos'/'required'/'parent_id' — all ALSO real nf3_fields columns, with byte-identical values in every row inspected). This is Ninja Forms' own internal redundancy (its model layer merges column + meta into one flat settings array — Abstracts/Model.php/ModelFactory.php), not a Duo design choice, and this manifest does not try to deduplicate it: both the column and its meta mirror are captured and replayed verbatim, exactly as the plugin itself maintains them. Attempting to omit the redundant meta copy would be a subtractive 'cleanup' this project's byte-fidelity discipline explicitly does not attempt.

The dual key/value + meta_key/meta_value column pair on all three _meta tables (verified via DESCRIBE, not assumed from the R1-A report's phrasing) is confirmed, on every real row inspected, to hold byte-identical content in both pairs — a back-compat artifact Ninja Forms' own write path (Database/Models/*.php) maintains by writing both simultaneously. This manifest reads from meta_key/meta_value (the 'current' pair, key_column/value_column) and WRITES both pairs on apply (legacy_key_column/legacy_value_column: key/value) to match what the plugin's own code does, rather than silently letting the legacy pair go stale.

The nf3_upgrades cache hazard (task #75's #5, reproduced empirically in docs/grind/r1a-forms.md: an id-reused form silently serves the PREVIOUS form's stale cached settings) is fixed via a per-row 'invalidate' declaration on nf3_forms, NOT a wp-cli rebuilder (Ninja Forms ships none — 'wp help nf' fails, confirmed again for this task) and NOT a proactively-rebuilt cache (unnecessary — see below). Traced to Ninja Forms' own source rather than guessed: WPN_Helper::delete_nf_cache($id) (includes/Helper.php) does exactly `DELETE FROM nf3_upgrades WHERE id=$id` + `delete_option('nf_form_'.$id)` (a legacy pre-table cache, confirmed empty of nf_form_* options on this fixture but declared defensively anyway), and its own read site (Abstracts/ModelFactory.php's constructor: `if ($form_cache && isset($form_cache['settings'])) { ... }`) correctly falls through to a FRESH read straight from nf3_forms/nf3_fields the moment the cache is simply ABSENT — confirmed by reading the exact conditional, not by trial and error. So invalidating (not rebuilding) after every apply-time write to a form's own row is sufficient: `"invalidate": [{"table": "nf3_upgrades", "column": "id"}, {"option_pattern": "nf_form_{id}"}]`.

The genuinely good news, unchanged from Grind R1-A and still true: submissions do NOT live in these custom tables. nf_sub posts (ordinary wp_postmeta) already round-trip through Duo's existing post/postmeta machinery; nf3_objects/nf3_object_meta/nf3_relationships were confirmed EMPTY of submission data in that round and stay classified runtime here, defensively. nf3_chunks: no FK-shaped column, no confirmed authored content — runtime.
nf_sub stays classified runtime here as a defensive backstop; the real protection is that site.duo.json's policy.post_types must never list it (visitor-submitted, never site-builder-authored).

The block_attrs entry above closes the OTHER half of task #75's acceptance criteria (a page embedding the form via block must render/submit correctly on the target — confirmed empirically live-wired, not by inspection alone: capturing the Careers fixture page BEFORE this entry existed left `{"formID":1,...}` as a raw, unrewritten local id — task #76's fixed regex correctly flagged it as unregistered_block_attr, exactly as intended). `"kind": "nf3_form"` resolves through the SAME generalized Tokens::id_to_token()/token_to_id() this manifest's table refs already use — Blocks.php never hardcoded which kinds are valid, so no engine change beyond Tokens.php's own generalization was needed for a block attribute to reference a table's id_kind. A real ordering hazard surfaced wiring this live, worth recording: Capture::build() runs table capture (which mints nf3_form identity into duo_map) BEFORE building any post body — capturing tables only AFTER post bodies would leave formID silently unrewritten even with this rule declared, since Tokens::id_to_token() would find no ledger entry yet.

`nf3_actions.active` and `nf3_fields.order` are declared `lint_ok: true` deliberately, not to silence noise blindly: both are small integers that coincide with real post/term ids on any small test fixture (order=1..23 walks straight through this site's own post ids 1-16; active=1 matches term id 1, 'Uncategorized') — reviewed and confirmed genuinely NOT refs (active is a boolean 0/1 flag; order is the field/action's own display position within its form, both plain WooCommerce.json-style audited exemptions, the same escape hatch as woocommerce.json's `queryId`).

Every BIT(1) boolean column (nf3_forms.show_title/clear_complete/hide_complete/logged_in, nf3_fields.required/personally_identifiable) is ALSO declared `lint_ok: true`, proactively rather than reactively: their only two possible values are 0/1, which WILL eventually coincide with some real entity's small id on some fixture (confirmed live: this manifest's own conformance-scale test site tripped show_title/clear_complete/hide_complete against term id 1 the first time this was wired end-to-end) — marking the whole COLUMN, not chasing whichever specific collision today's data happens to produce, is the correct, stable exemption for a column whose value space structurally excludes ever holding a ref.

Task #76 (Lint's looks_like_id_attr()/looks_like_id_key() missing the all-caps 'ID' suffix, e.g. Ninja Forms' own Gutenberg block attribute 'formID') is CLOSED separately (agent/src/Lint.php) — this manifest declares no block_attrs entry of its own because 'formID' now matches the fixed heuristic directly; nothing manifest-level was ever needed for that specific finding once the regex was widened.
